front_blocks.md: Give three things a higher bandwidth can improve.

back_blocks.md: Higher bandwidth improves **upload and download speeds**, **online gaming** and **streaming high definition video**.

back_blocks.md: A buffer is a **temporary area of memory** holding enough downloaded data to play a few seconds of streamed content.

cards.back_md: A buffer is a **temporary area of memory** holding enough downloaded data to play a few seconds of streamed content.

front_blocks.md: What condition must be met for content to stream successfully?

back_blocks.md: Data must be downloaded to the buffer **at a faster rate than it is being emptied**, otherwise the buffer empties and **playback will pause**.

front_blocks.md: Why does a large delay between data being sent and received increase the error rate?

back_blocks.md: A big delay means **more data will be on the network causing collisions**, which leads to **even more packets being sent** as the error rate increases.

cards.front_md: Why does a large delay between data being sent and received increase the error rate?

front_blocks.md: How does high latency affect a user playing a fast paced online game?

back_blocks.md: High latency causes **lag**, so the game does **not respond as quickly** to the user's commands, putting them at a disadvantage against players with lower latency.

front_blocks.md: How does high latency affect a video call?

back_blocks.md: It **increases the time it takes for data to be transferred between devices**, so voice and video become **out of sync, lagging or delayed**.

front_blocks.md: Compare wired and wireless connections on security and portability.

back_blocks.md: Wired has **better physical security** but its location is **limited by the physical cable**, while wireless is **less secure and easier to intercept** but its location is **only limited by range**.

front_blocks.md: Give three advantages of fibre optic over copper cable.

back_blocks.md: Fibre transmits data at a **much higher speed** with a **much higher bandwidth**, **does not suffer from interference** so is the most secure option for sensitive data, and can **cover long distances without degradation**.

front_blocks.md: Give two drawbacks of copper cable.

back_blocks.md: Copper **degrades over time**, which limits its range, and it **suffers from interference**, which can disrupt data quality; it is also **slower with lower bandwidth** than fibre.
